customer-acme: Hey team — getting 400 from /v1/rerank for a batch request that used to work. No body details in response, just 400.
meera_s: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact request body (or cURL) you used? 400 usually means malformed JSON or wrong types.
customer-acme: sure: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=ISO-2022-JP' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxx' -d '{"payload":"[{\"id\":1,\"candidates\":{\"a\":\"text1\"}}]' }'``` — we wrap the items on our side in a string because of legacy pipeline.
alex_k: ahh the payload looks stringified + envelope mismatch. Our API expects top-level items array of objects, not a string. Also candidates should be an array. That will cause parse failure and 400.
customer-acme: hmm we thought the server would accept an envelope key like `payload` — our SDK auto-wraps. Is `payload` explicitly unsupported?
jordan_tm: Correct — current contract: POST body must be JSON with `items: [{"id":"...","query":"...","candidates": [ {"id":"...","text":"..."} ]}]` and optional `top_k` int. Any deviation (string instead of array, object instead of array) -> 400.
meera_s: Can you try one minimal example without string-wrapping? e.g. ```{\n  \"items\": [ { \"id\": \"1\", \"query\": \"find best\", \"candidates\": [ { \"id\": \"c1\", \"text\": \"candidate text\" } ] } ]}```
customer-acme: ok reproducing now... also noticed we send Content-Type with charset; could that matter?
alex_k: Maybe — but JSON parsers usually ignore charset. The bigger issue is value types. That said, some proxies choke on unexpected charset metadata and strip or re-encode bodies which can corrupt bytes. One of our logs showed `Unexpected EOF` when charset was present behind certain proxies.
customer-acme: here's the failing body we captured from the client (base64 clipped): `eyJwYXlsb2FkIjoiW3tcImlkXCI6MVwiLCJjYW5kaWRhdGVzXCI6e30sIlRleHQiOnRydWV9XX0=` — looks like double-encoded.
jordan_tm: That base64 -> when decoded still contains a string around the array. So the client double-encodes. You need to send raw JSON not stringified JSON.
meera_s: Quick repro curl you can use locally (works): ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"items":[{"id":"1","query":"q","candidates":[{"id":"c1","text":"t1"}]}]}'``` If that succeeds, the issue is on their SDK/envelope layer.
customer-acme: running that now... getting 200 with scores. Good.
alex_k: Great. For a patch: remove the envelope/stringification step in your publish flow. You can also add a preflight validation hook that asserts `typeof body.items === 'object'` and `Array.isArray(body.items)`.
customer-acme: one more odd case — some older requests had `top_k: "3"` (string). Will that cause 400 or just coerce?
jordan_tm: We strictly validate types. `top_k` must be integer, sending string will trigger 400 with message "invalid type for top_k" in debug logs. We can check request id if you share one.
customer-acme: request id 01H8Q2ZZC3 — saw 400 at 2024-11-02T14:12:02Z.
ingest-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-8274 — Support ticket linked to request 01H8Q2ZZC3.
meera_s: I'll add a short remediation doc in the ticket and ping if we see anything else. For now: remove stringified envelope, send Content-Type without odd charset, ensure candidates is an array and top_k is integer. :thumbsup:
